reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that discrete event counts in sports—like goals or strikes—are often well-modeled by Poisson processes. However, real-world data frequently exhibits overdispersion or underdispersion, necessitating extensions such as the Conway-Maxwell-Poisson (CMP) model. For correlated outcomes, bivariate Poisson models or Skellam distributions provide more accurate joint probability estimates. These primitives form the foundation for probabilistic forecasting engines like GSE’s, where calibrated uncertainty is essential. Hierarchical Bayesian inference allows robust parameter estimation even when data is limited, especially useful in niche sports or new leagues. The failure mode occurs when these assumptions break down—e.g., non-stationary scoring patterns or extreme outliers—which requires dynamic model adaptation or hybrid approaches.
